findings.description: The policy grants ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, and cloudwatch:* on Resource "*", which is effectively broad administrative access across four services. This violates least privilege and lets the principal read/modify/delete virtually any data or compute resource in the account, including exfiltrating all S3 objects and altering security-relevant configuration.

A static IAM access key is issued for the svc_deploy user. Static keys do not expire and remain valid until manually rotated or deleted, making them a durable credential-theft target; the guidance calls for federation/temporary credentials instead.

findings.issue_category: long-lived IAM user instead of role
findings.description: A dedicated IAM user is created to hold programmatic permissions rather than a role with temporary credentials. Combined with force_destroy = true, the user (and any residual access) can be torn down or recreated without an-approval trail, and there is no permission boundary or guardrail limiting what this user can delegate.

The access key secret is emitted as a non-sensitive Terraform output. Outputs are stored in state and displayed in CLI/CI logs, so the key material leaks to anyone with read access to state or logs — a much wider audience than the secret store.
